{"assignees":[],"body":"## Problem\n\n`tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts:97` (\"repo topics can be added and removed by keyboard\") failed in Chromium on both e2e runs since Nov 14 that weren't skipped, while the other 308 tests passed:\n\n- [43685760783](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43685760783) (#183) and [43685766425](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43685766425) (#184), both on 2026-11-15, both at the same line:\n\n  ```\n  Locator: locator('#topic_edit .menu &gt; .item').filter({ hasText: 'beta' }).first()\n  Expected: visible   Timeout: 20000ms   Error: element(s) not found\n  ```\n\n- The same test passed in Firefox and WebKit in both runs.\n- The last e2e run before them, [43540800387](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43540800387) on `13f40966` (2026-11-14), passed all 309.\n\nWhat I ruled out:\n\n- **Code changes.** Between `13f40966` and the failing runs, no product code changed, only CI workflows, docs, mutation reports and one Vitest file. The e2e workflow changes from #182 (new triggers, an empty-on-PR `ref` input, a job timeout) don't change how a PR run behaves.\n- **Browser or Go version.** Both the passing and the failing runs used Chromium 158.0.8127.18 (Playwright chromium v1254) and Go 1.26.4. The runner image did change, from `ubuntu26/20261101.186` to `ubuntu26/20261111.196`.\n- **Local reproduction.** On macOS the test passes alone in all three browsers (12/12), in the Chromium project (104/104) and in the full suite with 5 workers (309 passed, 3 skipped).\n\nWhat's left: after `#manage_topic` is clicked and `beta` typed, the menu never gets an item. The menu fills only when the throttled `/explore/topics/search` request returns (`web_src/js/features/repo-home.ts`), so either the keystrokes never reached `input.search`, or that request failed or never fired. CI can't tell which. `playwright.config.ts` sets no `trace` or `retries`, the e2e job uploads no artifacts, so the `error-context.md` Playwright writes is thrown away, and the server log doesn't record requests.\n\nThis affects everyone. Once #182 merges, `e2e-tests` runs on every push to `main`, and any backend or frontend PR runs it too, so this test turns `main` and those PRs red until it's fixed.\n\n## Goal\n\nA failing e2e test in CI leaves a trace to debug from. The topics test passes reliably in CI, with its root cause found and fixed, not hidden.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n- [ ] AC1: Given an e2e run in CI where a test fails, when the job ends, then `tests/e2e-output/` (including `error-context.md` and a Playwright trace of the failed test) is uploaded as a workflow artifact kept for at most 7 days. Passing tests record no trace.\n- [ ] AC2: Given the AC1 artifact from a failing CI run, then the root cause of the topics failure is posted on this issue, naming which step fails (keyboard focus, the topic search request, or something else) and why it happens only in CI Chromium.\n- [ ] AC3: Given the fix, when `test-e2e` runs 10 times in CI, then the topics test passes all 10 times in all three browsers. Before the fix, 10 runs show how often it fails.\n- [ ] AC4: The fix keeps every assertion in the test. It doesn't skip the test, retry it, or raise its timeout beyond the 20 s it already has.\n\n## Evidence of Fix\n\nFlaky or failing test: the root cause (AC2) and 10 CI runs before and after the fix (AC3), with run links and pass/fail counts per browser. The before runs come from the AC1 change, so each failure in them has a trace.\n\n## Design Decision\n\n### Decision 1: get a trace out of CI before fixing anything\n\n**Decision:** Set `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` in `playwright.config.ts` when `CI` is set, and add an `actions/upload-artifact` step to `test-e2e` with `if: failure()` that uploads `tests/e2e-output/` with `retention-days: 7`. Fix the test only once the trace shows the cause.\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- *Guess and fix now*, for example by waiting for the search response before asserting. The failure doesn't reproduce locally, so there would be no way to confirm the guess fixed the cause rather than hid it, and the course counts silencing as small at most.\n- *Add `retries: 2` in CI.* It would turn `main` green, but it hides this failure and any later one.\n- *Debug on a runner over SSH (tmate).* It needs a third-party action with access to the runner, and it only helps while someone is watching.\n**Rationale:** Every later e2e failure in CI gets a trace too, not just this one, and the AC2 diagnosis comes from evidence.\n**Consequences:** A failed run uploads a few MB of traces, which counts toward the repo's artifact storage for 7 days. Traces of failing tests include page content from the e2e server's test data only.\n\n## Scope\n\nsmall, `scope: small`. AC1 is about 10 lines of config and workflow. The fix is probably small too, a wait or focus change in the test or in `repo-home.ts`, but AC2 may show otherwise; if so I'll re-scope here before starting the fix.\n\n---\n_Drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) for @controlled-opposition._\n","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAAC0JZuhA","name":"scope: small","description":"","color":"1aa89f"}],"milestone":null,"title":"test(e2e): repo topics keyboard test fails in CI Chromium and leaves nothing to debug"}

--- Jack-Donohue 2026-11-17T22:00:31Z
Spec reviewed — @Jack-Donohue

**Format:** The hardening task format fits: this is a failing CI test, and no product defect has been found yet. All six sections are there. The Design Decision has three concrete alternatives, a rationale and consequences, so it meets D3. I checked the Problem's claims against the repo and they hold: `playwright.config.ts` sets no `trace` or `retries`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` uploads nothing, the 20 s timeout is the 5 s `expect` timeout × the CI factor of 4 in `tools/test-e2e.sh`, and the topic search is throttled to 500 ms in `repo-home.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- **AC1:** Clear and testable from a failing run's artifact list and retention. One wording fix: `retain-on-failure` records a trace for every test and deletes it when the test passes, so the testable claim is "passing tests *keep* no trace."
- **AC2:** This is a diagnosis, not pass/fail behavior, but a flaky-test hardening issue needs the root cause as evidence, so it's fine. To make it checkable, say the comment must link the run and its artifact and quote the trace evidence: the `/explore/topics/search` network entry, or which element had focus while `beta` was typed.
- **AC3:** Testable, but it doesn't say how the 10 runs get triggered. Today `e2e-tests` only runs on `pull_request`. "Run workflow" comes with #182, which is still open. Please name the mechanism (re-running the jobs on your PR, or a dispatch after #182 merges) and list #182 as a dependency if you need it. Also, AC1 changes the config for all 309 tests, so add that the after-fix runs introduce no other new failures. The team can't introduce new failures this sprint.
- **AC4:** Clear and checkable from the diff. Please also rule out raising the timeout indirectly: `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` or the global `expect.timeout` would do it without touching the test.

**Cases considered:**
- *The failure doesn't show up in the 10 before-runs.* Tracing changes timing, and the runner image may change again. This isn't covered, and if it happens AC2 and AC3 can't pass. Please say now what happens then. For example: report 0/10 as the before count, keep the AC1 change as the deliverable, and re-scope or close.
- *Job time:* recording traces for 309 tests × 3 browsers adds overhead, and the job has `timeout-minutes: 10`. Worth checking in AC1 that the job still finishes well within that limit, compared with a run from before the change.
- *A cancelled run:* with `cancel-in-progress`, `failure()` is false, so nothing is uploaded. That's fine, because a cancelled run isn't a test failure.
- *The root cause is in `repo-home.ts`, not the test:* AC4 allows either fix, and the existing test already fails before and passes after, so this is covered.
- *Firefox and WebKit:* covered by AC3's "all three browsers."
- *Artifact contents:* traces will include the `e2e-admin` [REDACTED:generic-password] and API token. Both belong to a throwaway server on the runner, so there's no risk, but the Consequences line ("page content from test data only") should say so.

**Scope:** Small fits. AC1 is about 10 lines and the fix is likely small. The 20 CI runs take wall-clock time but little code. I agree with re-scoping here if AC2 turns up more.

**Issue metadata (D1):** The issue has no assignee, milestone or `type:` label. Please assign yourself as the owner, and add the `Sprint 3` milestone and a `type:` label.

**Verdict:** Changes needed:
1. Assign yourself, and add the `Sprint 3` milestone and a `type:` label.
2. AC3: name how the runs are triggered, note the #182 dependency, and add "no other new failures."
3. Add what happens if the before-runs don't reproduce the failure.
4. AC4: also forbid raising the timeout factor or the global `expect` timeout.
5. AC1: change "record no trace" to "keep no trace."

They're all small.

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {defineConfig, devices} from '@playwright/test';

const timeoutFactor = Number(env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR) || 1;
const timeout = 5000 * timeoutFactor;

export default defineConfig({
  workers: '50%',
  fullyParallel: true,
  testDir: './tests/e2e/',
  outputDir: './tests/e2e-output/',
  testMatch: /.*\.test\.ts/,
  forbidOnly: Boolean(env.CI),
  reporter: 'list',
  timeout: 2 * timeout,
  expect: {
    timeout,
  },
  use: {
    baseURL: env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_URL?.replace?.(/\/$/, ''),
    locale: 'en-US',
    actionTimeout: timeout,
    navigationTimeout: 2 * timeout,
  },
  projects: [
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
        permissions: ['clipboard-read', 'clipboard-write'],
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'firefox',
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Firefox'],
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'webkit',
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Safari'],
      },
    },
  ],
});


wf:
name: e2e-tests

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main] # #181: every suite runs on every merge, docs-only ones included
    tags: ["v*-csci435-*"] # sprint tags
  workflow_dispatch: # run the suites against any ref, e.g. an old sprint tag
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: Branch, tag or commit SHA to test
        required: true
        type: string

concurrency:
  # PRs keep their per-branch group; main shares one group so a newer merge only replaces the waiting run; each tag and manual run has its own (#181)
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' &amp;&amp; github.head_ref || github.event_name == 'push' &amp;&amp; github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &amp;&amp; github.ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  files-changed:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/files-changed.yml

  test-e2e:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.files-changed.outputs.backend == 'true' || needs.files-changed.outputs.frontend == 'true' || needs.files-changed.outputs.e2e == 'true'
    needs: files-changed
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }} # empty except on workflow_dispatch
      - uses: ./.github/actions/go-setup
      - uses: ./.github/actions/node-setup
      - run: make deps-frontend
      - run: make frontend
      - run: make deps-backend
      - run: make backend
        env:
          TAGS: bindata
      - run: make playwright
      - run: make test-e2e
        timeout-minutes: 10
        env:
          TAGS: bindata
          FORCE_COLOR: 1
          GITEA_TEST_E2E_DEBUG: 1

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-19 05:11:24Z)**_

The runs don't need a teammate. The only human step is approving each batch before it starts.

**Your part**
- **Approving each batch.** I can start the runs with your `gh` login (`gh workflow run pull-e2e-tests.yml --ref <branch> -f ref=<branch>`). Your instructions say to ask before each batch because every run takes one of the org's 20 runner slots for about 10 minutes.
- **Committing and pushing the AC1 change.** `--ref <branch>` runs the workflow file from that branch, so the trace and upload step has to be pushed there first. Every commit needs your approval.

**What runs without anyone**
- Manual runs don't cancel each other: each `workflow_dispatch` run gets its own concurrency group (`github.run_id`), and cancel-in-progress is only on for PRs.
- Org members don't need anyone to approve their workflow runs; that gate is only for outside contributors.
- The artifact upload needs no extra permissions, so `contents: read` is enough.
- I can watch the runs with `gh run watch`/`gh run view` and download the trace from a failed run with `gh run download`.

**Where teammates come in, outside the runs**
- **Jack's re-review of the spec**, before coding starts.
- **A teammate approving the latest commit of the PR** before you merge.
- **Runner slots:** 10 parallel runs could make teammates' CI wait in the queue tonight, before the deadline. A heads-up to the team, or starting the runs in smaller groups, would avoid that.

````markdown
## Problem

`tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts:97` ("repo topics can be added and removed by keyboard") failed in Chromium on both e2e runs since Nov 14 that weren't skipped, while the other 308 tests passed:

- [43685760783](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43685760783) (#183) and [43685766425](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43685766425) (#184), both on 2026-11-15, both at the same line:

  ```
  Locator: locator('#topic_edit .menu > .item').filter({ hasText: 'beta' }).first()
  Expected: visible   Timeout: 20000ms   Error: element(s) not found
  ```

- The same test passed in Firefox and WebKit in both runs.
- The last e2e run before them, [43540800387](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43540800387) on `13f40966` (2026-11-14), passed all 309.

What I ruled out:

- **Code changes.** Between `13f40966` and the failing runs, no product code changed, only CI workflows, docs, mutation reports and one Vitest file. The e2e workflow changes from #182 (new triggers, an empty-on-PR `ref` input, a job timeout) don't change how a PR run behaves.
- **Browser or Go version.** Both the passing and the failing runs used Chromium 158.0.8127.18 (Playwright chromium v1254) and Go 1.26.4. The runner image did change, from `ubuntu26/20261101.186` to `ubuntu26/20261111.196`.
- **Local reproduction.** On macOS the test passes alone in all three browsers (12/12), in the Chromium project (104/104) and in the full suite with 5 workers (309 passed, 3 skipped).

What's left: after `#manage_topic` is clicked and `beta` typed, the menu never gets an item. The menu fills only when the throttled `/explore/topics/search` request returns (`web_src/js/features/repo-home.ts`), so either the keystrokes never reached `input.search`, or that request failed or never fired. CI can't tell which. `playwright.config.ts` sets no `trace` or `retries`, the e2e job uploads no artifacts, so the `error-context.md` Playwright writes is thrown away, and the server log doesn't record requests.

This affects everyone. Once #182 merges, `e2e-tests` runs on every push to `main`, and any backend or frontend PR runs it too, so this test turns `main` and those PRs red until it's fixed.

## Goal

A failing e2e test in CI leaves a trace to debug from. The topics test passes reliably in CI, with its root cause found and fixed, not hidden.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given an e2e run in CI where a test fails, when the job ends, then `tests/e2e-output/` (including `error-context.md` and a Playwright trace of the failed test) is uploaded as a workflow artifact kept for at most 7 days. Passing tests keep no trace. The `test-e2e` job still finishes well within its 10-minute step limit, compared with a run from before the change.
- [ ] AC2: Given the AC1 artifact from a failing CI run, then the root cause of the topics failure is posted on this issue with a link to the run and its artifact, quoting the trace evidence (the `/explore/topics/search` network entry, or which element had focus while `beta` was typed), naming which step fails (keyboard focus, the topic search request, or something else) and why it happens only in CI Chromium.
- [ ] AC3: Given the fix, when `test-e2e` is started 10 times with `workflow_dispatch` (`gh workflow run pull-e2e-tests.yml -f ref=<branch>`, available since #182), then the topics test passes all 10 times in all three browsers and no other test fails that passed before. Before the fix, 10 dispatched runs with the AC1 change show how often it fails.
- [ ] AC4: The fix keeps every assertion in the test. It doesn't skip the test, retry it, or raise its timeout beyond the 20 s it already has, directly or through `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` or the global `expect.timeout`.

## Evidence of Fix

Flaky or failing test: the root cause (AC2) and 10 CI runs before and after the fix (AC3), with run links and pass/fail counts per browser. The before runs come from the AC1 change, so each failure in them has a trace.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: get a trace out of CI before fixing anything

**Decision:** Set `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` in `playwright.config.ts` when `CI` is set, and add an `actions/upload-artifact` step to `test-e2e` with `if: failure()` that uploads `tests/e2e-output/` with `retention-days: 7`. Fix the test only once the trace shows the cause.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Guess and fix now*, for example by waiting for the search response before asserting. The failure doesn't reproduce locally, so there would be no way to confirm the guess fixed the cause rather than hid it, and the course counts silencing as small at most.
- *Add `retries: 2` in CI.* It would turn `main` green, but it hides this failure and any later one.
- *Debug on a runner over SSH (tmate).* It needs a third-party action with access to the runner, and it only helps while someone is watching.
**Rationale:** Every later e2e failure in CI gets a trace too, not just this one, and the AC2 diagnosis comes from evidence.
**Consequences:** A failed run uploads a few MB of traces, which counts toward the repo's artifact storage for 7 days. Traces of failing tests include page content from the e2e server's test data only. They also contain the `e2e-admin` [REDACTED:generic-password] and API token, which belong to a throwaway server on the runner.

## Scope

small, `scope: small`. AC1 is about 10 lines of config and workflow. The fix is probably small too, a wait or focus change in the test or in `repo-home.ts`, but AC2 may show otherwise; if so I'll re-scope here before starting the fix. If none of the 10 before-runs fails, I'll report 0/10 as the before count, keep the AC1 change as the deliverable, and re-scope or close this issue here, since AC2 and AC3 can't be met without a failure.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

CONTAINER_RUNTIME="${CONTAINER_RUNTIME:-docker}"
CONTAINER_NAME="gitea-e2e-runner-$$"

free_port() {
  node -e "const s=require('net').createServer();s.listen(0,'127.0.0.1',()=&gt;{process.stdout.write(String(s.address().port));s.close()})"
}

detect_playwright_mode() {
  if [ "${PLAYWRIGHT_MODE:-auto}" = "local" ] || [ "${PLAYWRIGHT_MODE:-auto}" = "container" ]; then
    return
  fi

  PLAYWRIGHT_MODE="local"

  if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Linux" ]; then
    # playwright only supports ubuntu/debian officially
    if ! grep -qE '^ID(_LIKE)?=.*(ubuntu|debian)' /etc/os-release 2&gt;/dev/null; then
        PLAYWRIGHT_MODE="container"
    fi
  fi
}

wait_for_container() {
  local max_wait=30
  local elapsed=0
  echo "Waiting for container to start..."
  while ! (echo &gt; "/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$PLAYWRIGHT_SERVER_PORT") 2&gt;/dev/null; do
    if [ "$("$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$CONTAINER_NAME" 2&gt;/dev/null)" != "true" ]; then
      echo "Error: container exited before becoming ready." &gt;&amp;2
      "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" logs "$CONTAINER_NAME" &gt;&amp;2 || true
      return 1
    fi
    if [ "$elapsed" -ge "$max_wait" ]; then
      echo "Error: container did not become ready after ${max_wait}s." &gt;&amp;2
      "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" logs "$CONTAINER_NAME" &gt;&amp;2 || true
      return 1
    fi
    sleep 1
    elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
  done
  echo "Container is ready."
}

CMD="${1:-run}"
if [ "$CMD" = "install" ] || [ "$CMD" = "run" ]; then
  [ $# -gt 0 ] &amp;&amp; shift
else
  CMD="run"
fi

detect_playwright_mode

if [ "$PLAYWRIGHT_MODE" = "container" ]; then
  if ! command -v "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
    echo "error: PLAYWRIGHT_MODE=container but '$CONTAINER_RUNTIME' is not installed." &gt;&amp;2
    echo "Install docker/podman or set CONTAINER_RUNTIME to an available runtime." &gt;&amp;2
    exit 1
  fi
  PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION=$(sed -n 's/.*"@playwright\/test"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^[:digit:]]*\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' package.json)
  if ! [[ "$PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$ ]]; then
    echo "error: invalid @playwright/test version in package.json: '${PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION}'" &gt;&amp;2
    exit 1
  fi
  PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE="mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v${PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION}-noble"
fi

if [ "$CMD" = "install" ]; then
  if [ "$PLAYWRIGHT_MODE" = "local" ]; then
    # on GitHub Actions VMs, playwright's system deps are pre-installed for chromium and firefox
    if [ -z "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" ]; then
      # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # flag string
      pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox webkit ${PLAYWRIGHT_FLAGS:-}
    else
      # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # flag string
      pnpm exec playwright install chromium firefox ${PLAYWRIGHT_FLAGS:-}
      # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # flag string
      pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps webkit ${PLAYWRIGHT_FLAGS:-} # the runner image lacks webkit's gtk4/gstreamer libs
    fi
  else
    echo "Running playwright in container as host distro is not supported by playwright directly"
    if ! "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" image inspect "$PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE" &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
      "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" pull "$PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE"
    fi
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Create isolated work directory
WORK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)

# Find a random free port
FREE_PORT=$(free_port)

cleanup() {
  if [ "$PLAYWRIGHT_MODE" = "container" ]; then
    "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" stop "$CONTAINER_NAME" &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1 || true
  fi
  if [ -n "${SERVER_PID:-}" ]; then
    kill "$SERVER_PID" 2&gt;/dev/null || true
    wait "$SERVER_PID" 2&gt;/dev/null || true
  fi
  rm -rf "$WORK_DIR"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

if [ "$PLAYWRIGHT_MODE" = "container" ]; then
  PLAYWRIGHT_SERVER_PORT=$(free_port)
  # --network=host: container needs host loopback to reach gitea.
  "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" run --network=host --name "$CONTAINER_NAME" -d --rm --init --workdir /home/pwuser --user pwuser "$PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE" /bin/sh -c "npx -y playwright@${PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION} run-server --port ${PLAYWRIGHT_SERVER_PORT} --host 0.0.0.0"

  if ! wait_for_container; then
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# Write config file for isolated instance
mkdir -p "$WORK_DIR/custom/conf"
cat &gt; "$WORK_DIR/custom/conf/app.ini" &lt;&lt;EOF
[database]
DB_TYPE = sqlite3
PATH = $WORK_DIR/data/gitea.db

[server]
HTTP_PORT = $FREE_PORT
ROOT_URL = http://localhost:$FREE_PORT
STATIC_ROOT_PATH = $(pwd)

[security]
INSTALL_LOCK = true

[service]
ENABLE_CAPTCHA = false

[ui.notification]
EVENT_SOURCE_UPDATE_TIME = 500ms

[log]
MODE = console
LEVEL = Warn

[markup.test-external]
ENABLED = true
FILE_EXTENSIONS = .external
RENDER_COMMAND = cat
IS_INPUT_FILE = false
RENDER_CONTENT_MODE = iframe
EOF

export GITEA_WORK_DIR="$WORK_DIR"
export GITEA_TEST_E2E=true

# Start Gitea server
echo "Starting Gitea server on port $FREE_PORT (workdir: $WORK_DIR)..."
if [ -n "${GITEA_TEST_E2E_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
  "./$EXECUTABLE" web &amp;
else
  "./$EXECUTABLE" web &gt; "$WORK_DIR/server.log" 2&gt;&amp;1 &amp;
fi
SERVER_PID=$!

# Wait for server to be reachable
E2E_URL="http://localhost:$FREE_PORT"
MAX_WAIT=120
ELAPSED=0
while ! curl -sf --max-time 5 "$E2E_URL" &gt; /dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; do
  if ! kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2&gt;/dev/null; then
    echo "error: Gitea server process exited unexpectedly. Server log:" &gt;&amp;2
    cat "$WORK_DIR/server.log" 2&gt;/dev/null &gt;&amp;2 || true
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$ELAPSED" -ge "$MAX_WAIT" ]; then
    echo "error: Gitea server not reachable after ${MAX_WAIT}s. Server log:" &gt;&amp;2
    cat "$WORK_DIR/server.log" 2&gt;/dev/null &gt;&amp;2 || true
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 2
  ELAPSED=$((ELAPSED + 2))
done

echo "Gitea server is ready at $E2E_URL"

GITEA_TEST_E2E_DOMAIN="e2e.gitea.com"
GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER="e2e-admin"
GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD="[REDACTED:generic-password]"
GITEA_TEST_E2E_EMAIL="$GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER@$GITEA_TEST_E2E_DOMAIN"

# Create admin test user
"./$EXECUTABLE" admin user create \
  --username "$GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER" \
  --[REDACTED:generic-password] "$GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD" \
  --email "$GITEA_TEST_E2E_EMAIL" \
  --must-change-[REDACTED:generic-password]=false \
  --admin

# timeout multiplier to make the tests pass on slow CI runners while using
# factor 1 on a fast local machine like a MacBook Pro M1+
if [ -z "${GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR:-}" ]; then
  if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
    GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR=4
  else
    GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR=1
  fi
fi

export GITEA_TEST_E2E_URL="$E2E_URL"
export GITEA_TEST_E2E_DOMAIN
export GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER
export GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD
export GITEA_TEST_E2E_EMAIL
export GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR

if [ "$PLAYWRIGHT_MODE" = "container" ]; then
  export PW_TEST_CONNECT_WS_ENDPOINT="ws://127.0.0.1:${PLAYWRIGHT_SERVER_PORT}/"
fi
pnpm exec playwright test "$@"

<result>---
name: commit-and-pr-conventions
description: "Non-obvious commit/PR details beyond AGENTS.md: the model-ID trailer form, PR screenshots and how to host them."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 69cfac2d-d6c1-4099-8daf-14b2a01d3b02
  modified: 2026-11-04T22:43:33.694Z
---

AGENTS.md has the base rules: Conventional Commits, the `Assisted-by:` trailer only, approval for each commit, and the issue number in the subject. Beyond those:

- **Trailer form:** `Assisted-by: Claude Code:&lt;session model id&gt;`, for example `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5`.
- **Editing a PR body:** `gh pr edit --body-file` replaces the whole body. Keep the `Closes #N` line and any image URLs.
- **Chores without an issue:** the team opens `chore/` PRs (e.g. #140, #142) with no issue, milestone, spec or issue number in the commit subject; they still need a teammate's approval. PR body section rules are in [[course-rules]].
- **No stacked PRs:** COURSE-WORKFLOW forbids basing a PR on another feature branch or merging one into another. For a dependent issue (#60 needs #57), build it locally on top of #57 without pushing; after #57 merges, rebase that unpushed work onto `main`, then push and open the PR.
- **`gh pr merge --delete-branch`** closes any PR based on the deleted branch instead of retargeting it (tested 2026-10-24). The course repo has `delete_branch_on_merge=false`.
- **Screenshots required:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` wants UI screenshots on PRs. Show "after" only for a new feature, and before and after otherwise.

Hosting screenshots:
- `gh` can't mint `github.com/user-attachments/...` URLs; only the web UI uploads there.
- Commit the images under `docs/sprint&lt;N&gt;/screenshots/` (since 2026-10-24). Not under `ai-logs/`: `.coderabbit.yaml`'s PR-description check fails any link into `ai-logs/`, screenshots included (it flagged PR #115; Sprint 1's #71/#74 predate the check).
- Reference them as `https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/&lt;full-commit-sha&gt;/&lt;path&gt;?raw=1`. Use the SHA as pushed: an amend or squash before the push changes it, and the old link 404s. Pin the SHA, not the branch, so the images survive branch deletion.

Taking screenshots (done for PR #71):
- Use headless Chromium with `colorScheme: 'light' | 'dark'` and `deviceScaleFactor: 2`, then `page.screenshot` with a `clip`.
- Read each image back to check the crop.
- Rebuild first, or the footer shows a stale version.
- After pushing, confirm each `?raw=1` URL returns 200 as an image.

**Why:** The course fork diverges from default attribution, and these screenshot details each cost a retry.
**How to apply:** Use with [[verify-skill]] for the capture. Commit identity is in [[course-repo-and-identity]].

----
chore(ai-log): add AI logs for #181 spec self-review and PR #182 testing (#181)

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-haiku-5-5
---
chore(ai-log): add AI logs for #181 (#181)

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-haiku-5-5
---
ci(actions): restore the newest gobuild cache and let seeder runs finish (#181)

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5
---
docs(students): move the SONAR_TOKEN note back to the SonarQube bullet (#181)

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5
---
ci(actions): run all suites on main, tags and dispatch; speed up backend PRs (#181)

Guard the upstream release workflows to go-gitea/gitea, run db-tests and
e2e-tests on pushes to main, v*-csci435-* tags and workflow_dispatch,
refresh the Go build cache on every push to main, split the gogit unit
pass into its own job, move Vitest coverage out of the sonarqube chain,
and give every PR job a timeout.

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5
---</result>
</event>

The AC1 change is ready on a new branch, `test/issue-186-e2e-trace`, branched from the latest `main`. It isn't committed yet.

- `.github/workflows/pull-e2e-tests.yml`: a new `actions/upload-artifact` step after `make test-e2e`. It runs only `if: failure()`, uses the same pinned SHA as `pull-db-tests.yml` (v7.0.2), uploads `tests/e2e-output/` as `e2e-output` and keeps it for 7 days.

- `CI=1`, multiselect-aria file in Chromium: 4/4 passed, and `tests/e2e-output/` held only `.last-run.json`, so passing tests keep no trace.
- `CI=1` with timeouts cut to force failures: all 4 failed, and each left a `trace.zip` and an `error-context.md`. That's the folder the new step uploads.
- I skipped `/verify` because this change only touches test and CI config.

test(e2e): keep a Playwright trace of failed tests in CI and upload it (#186)

failure leaves error-context.md and a trace to debug from.

Batch 2 also had no failures, which makes it 0 out of 10 before-runs. Every run passed 309 tests with 3 skipped, the topics test passed in all three browsers each time, and the upload step was skipped every time because nothing failed.

| Run | Suite time | Runner image |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 44467669723 | 4.5 min | 20261111.196.1 |
| 44467673791 | 3.8 min | 20261111.82.6 |
| 44467677289 | 5.5 min | 20261111.196.1 |
| 44467680648 | 3.7 min | 20261111.82.6 |
| 44467683718 | 5.4 min | 20261111.196.1 |

Across all 10 traced runs, `make test-e2e` took 3.7–5.5 min, inside its 10-minute limit. The two runs on image `82.6` spent 6.5 and 15 min in `make playwright` downloading browsers. That step has no limit of its own, only the job's 45 minutes, so it's not part of #186.

This triggers the fallback written into #186: report 0/10 as the before count, keep AC1 as the deliverable, and re-scope or close. AC2 and AC3 can't be met without a failure to trace.

I recommend re-scoping #186 to AC1 plus the 0/10 report, and having the PR close it. With e2e now running on every push to `main`, the next failure will upload its own trace. Whoever sees it opens a new issue that starts from that trace, which is what AC2 needed. Keeping #186 open would leave a Sprint 3 issue waiting on a failure that may not happen for weeks.

If you agree, I'll draft three things for you to review:
1. A comment on #186 with the 10 run links, the per-browser counts and the job-time comparison, re-scoping it to AC1.
2. The edit to the issue body that marks AC2 and AC3 as deferred.
3. The PR in course format, with Test Evidence and `Closes #186`, so it can be opened before tonight's 11:59 PM deadline.

# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, the team
references logs in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page,
D5; later sprint pages also accept the PR, and the issue comment satisfies both).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log. The
PR's Test Evidence section has its own **AI-written tests** line, which names the tests AI wrote or
changed and how you checked their expected values (`COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, "Pull request format").

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.

# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site &lt;https://csci-435-se.github.io/&gt;
(Sprints pages and Glossary) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI
session, uses the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in
`.github/` carry the same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 3

- **Dates:** Nov 3 – Nov 19, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Nov 19, 11:59 PM**, except
  the D7 check-in, due **Nov 12, 11:59 PM** together with at least one code PR of your own, open
  and ready for review or merged.
- **Focus:** testing, meaning how well the tests check what the code is supposed to do.
- **Points:** 100.
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D8) or no release (D9) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** anything the Sprint 3 page doesn't change comes from the Sprint 2 and
  Sprint 1 pages, and every Sprint 0 standard still applies.
- **Start early:** record the test baseline at the Sprint 2 tag (see D8), and get the mutation tool
  running on any existing file in your area (see D6) before your PRs are ready.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 3` milestone with every selected issue on it, each with a justified scope | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), spec-reviewed on the issue before coding | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue, with **at least two alternatives** | 5 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs, each with `## Test Evidence` and `## Tech Debt` sections | 20 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 5 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint3/&lt;github-username&gt;/` |
| D6 | Mutation testing on one issue's PR (CSCI 535: two) | 15 | Individual | `docs/sprint3/mutation/` |
| D7 | Mid-sprint check-in, linking a code PR | 5 | Individual | `docs/sprint3/checkin/&lt;github-username&gt;.md` |
| D8 | Sprint report, with a Suite health section | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint3/report.md` |
| D9 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s3` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D10 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

### Graded strictly this sprint

The Sprint 3 page lists these as the rules that cost the most points. Details are in the sections
named.

1. No merge without a teammate's approval on the PR's **latest commit** (Reviews, below).
2. A spec review comment on the issue that says what was checked (Spec review, under the issue
   formats).
3. Every code PR has `Closes #&lt;N&gt;`, and both the issue and the PR are on the `Sprint 3` milestone.
4. Real AI logs, linked from the issue (D5).
5. A Test Evidence table in every PR, with expected values not copied from the code's output
   (Pull request format).
6. Mutation testing with a tool, with before and after reports committed (Mutation testing (D6)).
7. The team introduces no new test failures. A skipped test or a disabled CI check needs a linked
   issue and a reason in a code comment (D8).
8. A sprint report that renders on GitHub and uses the Sprint 3 sections (D8).

### Deliverable notes

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Either load can be met with equivalent story points instead. Every
  issue has exactly **one** assignee. Unfinished Sprint 2 issues go into the backlog before new
  work. To drop one, write the reason on that issue. If the backlog is too thin to meet the load,
  find areas that still need work (features, improvements, test gaps, bugs) and write new issues
  for them the usual way.
- **D1 scope:** every issue states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences on why:
  which components it touches and how much change is expected. The instructor or TA may reclassify
  an issue whose scope is clearly overstated.
- **D1 hardening issues (optional):** one of your issues may be a hardening issue. See "Hardening
  issues" below.
- **D1 team feature:** the instructor or TA posts a larger feature for Sprints 3–4 as an issue and
  tells the team. Split it into sub-issues, each with one owner, its own spec (D2) and scope, linked
  to the feature issue and added to the `Sprint 3` milestone. Sub-issues count toward the load.
- **D2:** specs are written and spec-reviewed before coding starts. Features use the user story
  format; hardening issues use the bug report format when they fix a defect, otherwise the
  hardening task format.
- **D3:** each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and why one won; this is graded
  strictly. The site also accepts the decision in an issue comment or the PR description; the team
  keeps it in the issue body. Decisions that span issues go in `docs/sprint3/design.md`.
- **D4:** every PR description has the Test Evidence and Tech Debt sections (see "Pull request
  format"). Per-PR scores are combined across your PRs and scaled to 20.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. Logs hold the full prompts and output. Graded
  strictly this sprint: a session summary, paraphrased prompts, a share link, or tool output without
  the prompts that produced it is not a log. The link must open the log file itself, not a folder
  or another issue. The folder must exist even if no AI was used; in that case, post a comment
  saying so. The site accepts the link from the issue or the PR; the team keeps it in **issue
  comments only** (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D6:** see "Mutation testing (D6)" below.
- **D7:** about 100 words on each of: what you have implemented so far and what remains; one thing
  you learned about testing in the project; one risk to finishing by Nov 19 and what you will do
  about it. Link at least one **code PR you authored**, open and ready for review or merged, by Nov
  12. On time, substantive and with a PR linked scores 5; late, thin or no PR 3; missing 0.
- **D8:** graded on completeness, specificity, quality of evidence and the Suite health section;
  sections are in "Sprint report (D8) sections" below.
- **D9:** keep the base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s2` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s3`). Tag **after the
  last Sprint 3 merge**, so the release matches the final `main`, and push the tag to origin. The
  release description summarizes the sprint's features, fixes and hardening work, not just the tag
  name.
- **Reviews:** nobody approves or merges their own PR. Request the review on GitHub and tell the
  reviewer on Zulip; reviewers respond (approve or request changes) within 24 hours, with
  substantive comments and the rubric, not a bare approval. A PR is merged only after a teammate
  approves its **latest commit**: any push after the approval, including merging `main` in, needs
  a new approval. Once approved, the author merges. Each student reviews at least one PR per
  sprint, and every teammate at least once per semester.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR submitted to upstream Gitea that is accepted or under
  active review, and up to 2 points per bug report filed upstream that comes from your own testing
  and is confirmed by the maintainers by the time Sprint 4 is graded. Both at the instructor's
  discretion.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-&lt;N&gt;-short-description`, `fix/issue-&lt;N&gt;-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-&lt;N&gt;-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. A merge pushed after
approval needs a new approval (see Reviews). Never merge another feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once its latest commit is approved, every review comment is
addressed and CI passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-&lt;N&gt;-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-&lt;N&gt;-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), that the issue and PR are on the sprint
milestone, and that the issue has its AI Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the
session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

```markdown
## User Story
As a &lt;role&gt;, I want &lt;capability&gt; so that &lt;benefit&gt;.

## User Scenario
&lt;A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.&gt;

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given &lt;state&gt;, when &lt;action&gt;, then &lt;observable result&gt;.
- [ ] AC2: ...
- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)

## Out of Scope
- &lt;What this issue deliberately does not do.&gt;

## Open Questions
- &lt;Unresolved questions, or "None".&gt;

## Design Decision
**Decision:** &lt;what was chosen&gt;
**Alternatives Considered:** &lt;at least two concrete options, and why each lost&gt;
**Rationale:** &lt;why this one&gt;
**Consequences:** &lt;trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder&gt;

## Scope
small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
&lt;One or two sentences on why: the components it touches and how much change you expect.&gt;
```

## Issue format: bug report

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`. Also used by hardening issues that fix a
defect.

```markdown
## Observed Behavior
## Expected Behavior
## Steps to Reproduce
1. ...
## Additional Information
&lt;Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.&gt;
## Design Decision
&lt;Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.&gt;
## Scope
&lt;Same as above: size, label and one or two sentences on why.&gt;
```

## Issue format: hardening task

No GitHub template; write it in a blank issue. Used by hardening issues that don't fix a defect,
such as a flaky test or a broken CI check (Sprint 3, D2).

```markdown
## Problem
&lt;What is unreliable now, and how you know: failing test names, run counts, CI run links.&gt;
## Goal
&lt;What "fixed" means.&gt;
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: ...
## Evidence of Fix
&lt;Which evidence from the table below the fix will show.&gt;
## Design Decision
&lt;Same four fields as above.&gt;
## Scope
&lt;Same as above: size, label and one or two sentences on why.&gt;
```

### Hardening issues

Work that makes the existing system more reliable rather than adding a feature. Good sources: the
D8 baseline run (failing or flaky tests, broken CI checks on `main`); the "Introduced" and
"Encountered" Tech Debt fields of Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs; bugs found in reviews or after
merging; and the upstream issue tracker for the parts of Gitea the team works on. It is scoped like
any other issue and must include evidence that the problem is fixed:

| Kind | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Bug fix | A test that fails before the fix and passes after |
| Flaky test | The root cause, and repeated runs before and after the fix (e.g. 20 for a unit test, 10 for E2E) |
| Broken or missing CI check | Links to CI runs before and after the fix |
| Failing tests in the baseline | Pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each group of failures |

The site doesn't say where the evidence goes: plan it in the issue (Evidence of Fix, or Additional
Information for a bug), then post the results on the issue and in the PR's Test Evidence once the
fix is in. Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause
counts as small at most.

### Design Decision and spec review

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Spec review (D2):** before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment **on the issue**.
  Start it with `Spec reviewed` so it is easy to find. The layout is the reviewer's choice, but the
  comment must say what was checked:
  1. each acceptance criterion: clear and testable, naming any that aren't;
  2. the cases considered (e.g. empty input, errors, permissions) and whether the ACs cover them;
  3. whether the scope fits the stated size;

  and end with an approval, or the problems for the author to fix in the spec. `Looks good!` with
  nothing about what was checked does not count. An optional layout:

  ```markdown
  Spec reviewed — @reviewer-username

  **Acceptance criteria:** &lt;clear and testable? which aren't, and why&gt;
  **Cases considered:** &lt;which cases, and whether the ACs cover them&gt;
  **Scope:** &lt;does it fit the stated size?&gt;
  **Verdict:** Approved | Changes needed: &lt;list&gt;
  ```

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #&lt;N&gt;`, which links the issue and closes it on merge. Every code PR links its issue, and
   the PR goes on the `Sprint 3` milestone too.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **Test Evidence:** required from Sprint 3. It replaces the old "How it was tested" section.
   Every behaviour change still needs a new or updated test.

   ```markdown
   ## Test Evidence

   | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |

   **Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]

   **AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
   ```

   - **One row per acceptance criterion** from the issue; for a bug report, the Expected Behavior.
     A PR that changes no product behaviour (e.g. a CI change) writes `N/A` and why.
   - **Test(s):** the test name, plus the file if not obvious. For a manual check, write `Manual:`
     followed by the steps and what you saw. An AC tested both ways lists both in the same row.
   - **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E` or `manual`.
   - **Source of expected value:** `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or
     `other` (explain). **Never the current output of your own code:** a test whose expected value
     was copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
   - **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
   - AI may draft this section; the author checks that it is accurate.

5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status. If CI doesn't run your tests, the commands you ran and
   a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** &lt;shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why&gt;

   **Encountered:** &lt;tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it&gt;
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6; tests written or updated
appropriately, with the Test Evidence section complete, every AC covered and expected values
justified 6; description explains what and why, Tech Debt section present, issue linked 3; CI passes
or manual verification documented 3; reviewed with the rubric (including the test evidence row),
reviewer comment posted, merged only after an approval on the latest commit 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** &lt;what you ran or tried&gt;

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Test evidence — does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## Mutation testing (D6)

A mutation testing tool makes small changes to the code (*mutants*), such as flipping a condition
or a boundary value, and runs the tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is
**killed**. If every test passes, it **survived**: the tests didn't notice the change, which points
to a weak or missing test. An **equivalent** mutant behaves exactly like the original code, so no
test can kill it. Definitions are in the course Glossary.

**Which issue:** one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two, and the
small issue may be one of them). A tool is required; mutating code by hand doesn't count.

| Code changed | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend TypeScript (Vitest) | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
| Go backend | Gremlins or go-mutesting |

1. Run the tool on the **source files changed by your PR(s)** for that issue, not the whole
   project.
2. Analyse every surviving mutant: equivalent, or a gap in your tests? If more than 10 survive,
   analyse at least 10, starting with lines your PR added or changed.
3. Add or strengthen **at least one test that kills a survivor** that revealed a gap, and re-run
   the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent), say so
   and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
4. Answer the three questions in the write-up.

Files:

- Write-up: `docs/sprint3/mutation/&lt;issue#&gt;-&lt;github-username&gt;.md`, using the template below.
- Reports: machine-readable output of the first run and the re-run, as
  `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/&lt;issue#&gt;-&lt;github-username&gt;-before.json` and `-after.json` (`.txt`
  for go-mutesting). StrykerJS: add `"json"` to `reporters`. Gremlins: `--output=&lt;file&gt;.json`.
  go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file. The scores in the write-up must match the
  reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.
- The tool configuration you used, committed and linked from the write-up. Reusing a teammate's
  setup is encouraged, as long as you run the tool yourself and credit them. The team's shared
  setup (go-mutesting for Go), its commands and its pitfalls: `.claude-students/docs/mutation-testing.md`.

Common problems:

- **The tool stops before mutating.** It first runs the selected tests on unchanged code and stops
  if any fail. Fix or exclude them first; the D8 baseline shows which ones fail already.
- **Tests run against built code.** Mutants in the source are never seen by tests that run on
  compiled output. Configure a rebuild, or pick tests that run on source.
- **Tests need services.** Start the database or service first. How each test type runs is in
  `.claude-students/docs/testing.md`.
- **False survivors.** When limiting which tests run, include the tests that cover the mutated
  files. Otherwise mutants they would catch show as survived or not covered. Check that the
  relevant tests ran before writing a new test for a survivor.
- **Blocked?** Ask teammates first. Then tell the TA **as early as possible**, with the errors and
  the AI log of what you tried; the TA may approve a different issue or area. Problems reported at
  the end of the sprint don't excuse a missing D6.

Template, copied from the Sprint 3 page:

```markdown
# Mutation testing: Issue #&lt;N&gt; -- &lt;issue title&gt;

**PR(s):** #...  **Tool:** ...  **Config:** [link; credit the teammate if you reused their setup]  **Command:** `...`
**Reports:** [before](reports/&lt;issue#&gt;-&lt;username&gt;-before.json) · [after](reports/&lt;issue#&gt;-&lt;username&gt;-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before ...% → after ...%

## Surviving mutants

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| | | | |

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [link] · Test: [file › test name] · Kills: [mutant location]

## Questions

1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?
2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.

and reports committed 4; surviving mutants analysed correctly (equivalent or test gap, with an
explanation) 4; at least one new or strengthened test kills a survivor, confirmed by the re-run 4;
answers show understanding, not just description 3. CSCI 535: the average of the two write-ups.

## Problem

`tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts:97` ("repo topics can be added and removed by keyboard") failed in Chromium on both e2e runs since Nov 14 that weren't skipped, while the other 308 tests passed:

- [43685760783](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43685760783) (#183) and [43685766425](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43685766425) (#184), both on 2026-11-15, both at the same line:

  ```
  Locator: locator('#topic_edit .menu > .item').filter({ hasText: 'beta' }).first()
  Expected: visible   Timeout: 20000ms   Error: element(s) not found
  ```

- The same test passed in Firefox and WebKit in both runs.
- The last e2e run before them, [43540800387](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43540800387) on `13f40966` (2026-11-14), passed all 309.

What I ruled out:

- **Code changes.** Between `13f40966` and the failing runs, no product code changed, only CI workflows, docs, mutation reports and one Vitest file. The e2e workflow changes from #182 (new triggers, an empty-on-PR `ref` input, a job timeout) don't change how a PR run behaves.
- **Browser or Go version.** Both the passing and the failing runs used Chromium 158.0.8127.18 (Playwright chromium v1254) and Go 1.26.4. The runner image did change, from `ubuntu26/20261101.186` to `ubuntu26/20261111.196`.
- **Local reproduction.** On macOS the test passes alone in all three browsers (12/12), in the Chromium project (104/104) and in the full suite with 5 workers (309 passed, 3 skipped).

What's left: after `#manage_topic` is clicked and `beta` typed, the menu never gets an item. The menu fills only when the throttled `/explore/topics/search` request returns (`web_src/js/features/repo-home.ts`), so either the keystrokes never reached `input.search`, or that request failed or never fired. CI can't tell which. `playwright.config.ts` sets no `trace` or `retries`, the e2e job uploads no artifacts, so the `error-context.md` Playwright writes is thrown away, and the server log doesn't record requests.

This affects everyone. Once #182 merges, `e2e-tests` runs on every push to `main`, and any backend or frontend PR runs it too, so this test turns `main` and those PRs red until it's fixed.

## Goal

A failing e2e test in CI leaves a trace to debug from. The topics test passes reliably in CI, with its root cause found and fixed, not hidden.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given an e2e run in CI where a test fails, when the job ends, then `tests/e2e-output/` (including `error-context.md` and a Playwright trace of the failed test) is uploaded as a workflow artifact kept for at most 7 days. Passing tests keep no trace. The `test-e2e` job still finishes well within its 10-minute step limit, compared with a run from before the change.
- [ ] AC2 (deferred, see the re-scope comment below): Given the AC1 artifact from a failing CI run, then the root cause of the topics failure is posted on this issue with a link to the run and its artifact, quoting the trace evidence (the `/explore/topics/search` network entry, or which element had focus while `beta` was typed), naming which step fails (keyboard focus, the topic search request, or something else) and why it happens only in CI Chromium.
- [ ] AC3 (deferred, see the re-scope comment below): Given the fix, when `test-e2e` is started 10 times with `workflow_dispatch` (`gh workflow run pull-e2e-tests.yml -f ref=<branch>`, available since #182), then the topics test passes all 10 times in all three browsers and no other test fails that passed before. Before the fix, 10 dispatched runs with the AC1 change show how often it fails.
- [ ] AC4: The fix keeps every assertion in the test. It doesn't skip the test, retry it, or raise its timeout beyond the 20 s it already has, directly or through `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` or the global `expect.timeout`.

## Evidence of Fix

Flaky or failing test: the root cause (AC2) and 10 CI runs before and after the fix (AC3), with run links and pass/fail counts per browser. The before runs come from the AC1 change, so each failure in them has a trace.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: get a trace out of CI before fixing anything

**Decision:** Set `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` in `playwright.config.ts` when `CI` is set, and add an `actions/upload-artifact` step to `test-e2e` with `if: failure()` that uploads `tests/e2e-output/` with `retention-days: 7`. Fix the test only once the trace shows the cause.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Guess and fix now*, for example by waiting for the search response before asserting. The failure doesn't reproduce locally, so there would be no way to confirm the guess fixed the cause rather than hid it, and the course counts silencing as small at most.
- *Add `retries: 2` in CI.* It would turn `main` green, but it hides this failure and any later one.
- *Debug on a runner over SSH (tmate).* It needs a third-party action with access to the runner, and it only helps while someone is watching.
**Rationale:** Every later e2e failure in CI gets a trace too, not just this one, and the AC2 diagnosis comes from evidence.
**Consequences:** A failed run uploads a few MB of traces, which counts toward the repo's artifact storage for 7 days. Traces of failing tests include page content from the e2e server's test data only. They also contain the `e2e-admin` [REDACTED:generic-password] and API token, which belong to a throwaway server on the runner.

## Scope

small, `scope: small`. AC1 is about 10 lines of config and workflow. The fix is probably small too, a wait or focus change in the test or in `repo-home.ts`, but AC2 may show otherwise; if so I'll re-scope here before starting the fix. If none of the 10 before-runs fails, I'll report 0/10 as the before count, keep the AC1 change as the deliverable, and re-scope or close this issue here, since AC2 and AC3 can't be met without a failure.

**Re-scoped 2026-11-19:** 0 of 10 before-runs failed, so this issue delivers AC1 (and the AC4 constraint, since no fix is made). AC2 and AC3 move to a new issue if the test fails again in CI, which will then leave a trace.

```markdown
Closes #186

## What changed

- `playwright.config.ts`: when `CI` is set, Playwright records a trace of each test and keeps it only if the test fails (`retain-on-failure`). Local runs don't record traces.
- `.github/workflows/pull-e2e-tests.yml`: when `test-e2e` fails, a new step uploads `tests/e2e-output/` (each failed test's `trace.zip` and `error-context.md`) as the `e2e-output` artifact, kept for 7 days. The action is pinned to the same SHA `pull-db-tests.yml` uses (v7.0.2).

## Why

The topics keyboard test failed twice in CI Chromium on Nov 15 and never locally, and CI kept nothing to debug it from. This PR covers AC1: any future e2e failure in CI leaves a trace. AC4 holds too: the test and its timeouts are unchanged, with no retries or skips.

I ran 10 `workflow_dispatch` runs with this change to catch the failure (AC2/AC3), and all 10 passed in all three browsers. Following the fallback in #186's Scope, the issue is re-scoped to AC1, and AC2/AC3 move to a new issue if the test fails again. Run links and counts are in the re-scope comment on #186.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: a failed CI test leaves `error-context.md` and a trace in a 7-day artifact; passing tests keep none | Manual, locally: `CI=1 GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts --project=chromium' make test-e2e` passed 4/4 and left only `.last-run.json` in `tests/e2e-output/`. The same command with `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR=0.02` failed 4/4 and left a `trace.zip` and `error-context.md` per test. CI proof run [44471025770](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44471025770), on a throwaway branch (since deleted) with `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR: 0.02` added to force the 4 multiselect-aria tests to fail: `make test-e2e` failed, the upload step ran, and the `e2e-output` artifact (105 KB, expires 2026-11-26, 7 days after upload) holds a `trace.zip` and `error-context.md` for each of the 12 failed tests. The 10 passing dispatched runs skipped the upload step (links on #186). | manual (local and CI) | AC, [Playwright `trace` docs](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-use-options#recording-options) |
| AC1: the job still finishes well within the 10-minute step limit | `make test-e2e` step took 3.9–5.7 min in the 10 runs, against 4.2 and 4.7 min in the two runs before the change | manual | AC |
| AC2: root cause | N/A, deferred: no failure in 10 runs (see #186) | — | — |
| AC3: 10 runs before and after a fix | Before: 0/10 failed. No fix was made, so there are no after runs; deferred (see #186) | — | — |
| AC4: no retries, skips or raised timeouts | The diff: no change to the test, `retries`, `expect.timeout` or `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` | manual | AC |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** AC1 is CI configuration, so it can't have an automated test. The upload step only runs when a test fails in CI and none failed in the 10 real runs, so it was proven with one forced-failure CI run and a forced-failure local run.

**AI-written tests:** None. No test files changed.

## CI / manual verification

`make lint-actions` and `eslint playwright.config.ts` pass. The 10 dispatched `e2e-tests` runs on this branch all passed (309 passed, 3 skipped each).

## Design

As in #186's Design Decision 1 (trace first, fix only from evidence). Unchanged.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** None. A failed run uploads a few MB of traces kept for 7 days. The traces include the throwaway `e2e-admin` [REDACTED:generic-password] and token.

**Encountered:** The topics test flake is still unexplained and may come back; it now leaves a trace when it does. `make playwright` took 6.5–15 min on runner image `20261111.82.6` (about 40 s on `20261111.196.1`) and has no step timeout. I left it alone because it's outside #186.

## Before-runs: 0 failures in 10, re-scoping to AC1

With the AC1 change on `test/issue-186-e2e-trace` (commit `b9d28990e5`), I started `test-e2e` 10 times with `workflow_dispatch`:

- Batch 1: [44465216451](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44465216451), [44465219747](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44465219747), [44465222984](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44465222984), [44465226300](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44465226300), [44465229778](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44465229778)
- Batch 2: [44467669723](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44467669723), [44467673791](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44467673791), [44467677289](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44467677289), [44467680648](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44467680648), [44467683718](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44467683718)

Every run passed: 104 tests in Chromium, 103 in Firefox, 102 in WebKit, 3 skipped. The topics test passed in all three browsers in all 10. The upload step was skipped each time because nothing failed, so there's no trace to diagnose from. Runners were on image `20261111.196.1` (7 runs) and `20261111.82.6` (3 runs), and the two failures on Nov 15 were on `20261111.196`, so the image alone doesn't trigger the failure.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Topics test failures, Chromium | 2 of the 2 PR runs on Nov 15 | 0/10 |
| `make test-e2e` step time | 4.2 and 4.7 min ([44455280225](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44455280225), [44458157446](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44458157446)) | 3.9–5.7 min |

Recording traces keeps the step well inside its 10-minute limit. To show the upload works on a real failure, I also ran [44471025770](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/44471025770) from a throwaway branch (since deleted) that forced the multiselect-aria tests to fail: it uploaded the `e2e-output` artifact, set to expire after 7 days, with a trace and `error-context.md` for each of the 12 failed tests.

Per the fallback in Scope, I'm reporting 0/10 as the before count and keeping the AC1 change as this issue's deliverable. AC2 and AC3 are deferred: they need a failure to trace, and 10 runs didn't produce one. Since #182, `e2e-tests` runs on every push to `main`, so the next time this test fails it uploads its own trace, and whoever sees it can open a new issue that starts from that trace and link this one.
